findings.title: LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice inverts lookback: spot returned for TWAP
findings.description:
LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice (contracts/libraries/Oracle/LibChainlinkOracle.sol#39-48) selects the price source with an INVERTED ternary:

    return lookback > 0
        ? getPrice(priceAggregatorAddress, maxTimeout)        // <-- instantaneous SPOT
        : getTwap(priceAggregatorAddress, maxTimeout, lookback); // <-- lookback==0 here

The semantics are backwards. The sibling oracle LibEthUsdOracle.getEthUsdPrice(lookback) (LibEthUsdOracle.sol#53-65) and the NatSpec everywhere in the codebase document the intended contract as: lookback > 0 => use the manipulation-resistant TWAP, lookback == 0 => use the instantaneous price. Here the two branches are swapped.

Consequences:
  (1) When a caller requests a TWAP (lookback > 0), getTokenPrice returns getPrice(...) — the single-round latestRoundData spot price — completely ignoring the requested averaging window. The manipulation-resistance the caller asked for is silently discarded.
  (2) When a caller requests the instantaneous price (lookback == 0), it calls getTwap(...,0). getTwap computes t.endTimestamp = block.timestamp - 0 = block.timestamp; the first `if (timestamp <= t.endTimestamp)` branch is taken (the latest round timestamp is <= now), so it returns the spot price via the early return and the final `.div(lookback)` (div-by-zero) is never reached. So the lookback==0 path happens to still return spot — but only by accident of the early return.

The net live bug is (1): every TWAP request through this function returns a non-time-averaged value. This function is the generic chainlink price path used by LibUsdOracle.getTokenPriceFromExternal for encodeType 0x01 tokens (LibUsdOracle.sol#120-127) and as the stablecoin leg of the uniswap+chainlink encodeType 0x02 path (LibUsdOracle.sol#155-160). ETH and WSTETH bypass getTokenPrice (LibUsdOracle.getUsdPrice/getTokenPrice branch on C.WETH / C.WSTETH and call LibEthUsdOracle/LibWstethUsdOracle directly, which use the CORRECT ternary), so the current BEAN:ETH / BEAN:wstETH wells are not affected. The exposure is any whitelisted Well whose non-Bean token resolves to the default chainlink implementation (encodeType 0x01), or any token whose USD value is fetched with a non-zero lookback for manipulation resistance.

location.code_snippet:
return
    lookback > 0
        ? getPrice(priceAggregatorAddress, maxTimeout)
        : getTwap(priceAggregatorAddress, maxTimeout, lookback);

findings.impact: For any whitelisted Well whose non-Bean token uses the default chainlink oracle (encodeType 0x01), the season minting oracle requests a TWAP (LibWellMinting.twaDeltaB -> LibWell.getRatiosAndBeanIndex(tokens, block.timestamp - season.timestamp) -> LibUsdOracle.getUsdPrice(token, lookback>0)) but receives the manipulable SPOT chainlink answer. The returned `ratios` feed calcReserveAtRatioSwap, which sets deltaB (LibWellMinting.sol#172-179) — the exact quantity of Beans minted in stepSun, and the soil/pod issuance derived from it. The same spot-for-twap substitution corrupts the LP-to-supply ratio (LibEvaluate.calcLPToSupplyRatio) and the excessive-price weather case (LibEvaluate.evalPrice). An attacker who skews the chainlink-priced token's spot feed (or sandwiches a thin feed update) at the season boundary biases the freshly minted supply distribution in their favour, defeating the TWA defense Beanstalk explicitly relies on.
findings.recommendation:
Swap the ternary branches so the function matches its documented and sibling-oracle semantics:

    return lookback > 0
        ? getTwap(priceAggregatorAddress, maxTimeout, lookback)
        : getPrice(priceAggregatorAddress, maxTimeout);

Add a regression test asserting that getTokenPrice(agg, timeout, 900) routes to getTwap and getTokenPrice(agg, timeout, 0) routes to getPrice. Consider reverting (rather than silently early-returning) inside getTwap when lookback == 0 to harden against future callers.

references.title: H-6: PerpDepository#getPositionValue uses incorrect value for TWAP interval allowing more than intended funds to be extracted (UXD Protocol)

ite.intent: Bias the per-season Bean mint / soil sizing by manipulating the spot chainlink price of a whitelisted Well's non-Bean token in the block sunrise reads it, profiting from the mispriced freshly-minted supply.
ite.technique: Permissionless sunrise()->gm()->stepOracle() runs LibWellMinting.twaDeltaB, which calls LibWell.getRatiosAndBeanIndex(tokens, nonzero-lookback) -> LibUsdOracle.getUsdPrice(token, lookback) -> getTokenPriceFromExternal (encodeType 0x01) -> LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice(agg, timeout, lookback>0). Because of the inverted ternary at LibChainlinkOracle.sol#44-46 this returns getPrice() (single-round spot) instead of the lookback TWAP. The spot value becomes `ratios`, which sets deltaB (LibWellMinting.sol#172) and hence uint256(deltaB) Beans minted in stepSun.
ite.evasion: The developer intended manipulation resistance via the TWA lookback (and correctly implemented it in LibEthUsdOracle/LibWstethUsdOracle). The gap is exactly the swapped branches in the generic chainlink helper LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice, which silently drops the averaging window for any token routed through the default chainlink implementation.

findings.human_review_reason: Exploit economics span the season boundary (multi-block oracle/minting reasoning) and the live impact is conditional on a Well being whitelisted whose non-Bean token uses the default chainlink (encodeType 0x01) oracle path; current BEAN:ETH/wstETH wells bypass the bug. Human must confirm the active whitelist and the feed-manipulability of any encodeType 0x01 token before finalizing severity.
critical_assumptions: A Well is whitelisted whose non-Bean token resolves to LibUsdOracle encodeType 0x01 (default chainlink) rather than the WETH/WSTETH special-case branches.
That token's chainlink spot feed is manipulable / sandwich-able at the season boundary enough to move deltaB profitably.

ice_chain.corrupted_state: ratios[] returned by LibWell.getRatiosAndBeanIndex -> deltaB in LibWellMinting.twaDeltaB
ice_chain.consumer_action: Mints uint256(deltaB) Beans (C.bean().mint) and sizes soil/pod issuance off the corrupted price

findings.title: LibWell USD/bean-price math hardcodes 18-decimal non-Bean token assumption
findings.description:
Several LibWell helpers scale Well reserves with hardcoded 1e18 / 1e6 factors that are only correct when the non-Bean token has 18 decimals. The functions even document the assumption ('assumes TKN has 18 decimals', LibWell.sol#178 and #216) but nothing enforces it on whitelist.

  - getWellTwaUsdLiquidityFromReserves (LibWell.sol#134-155): for the in-season path it returns twaReserves[j].mul(1e18).div(tokenUsd) where tokenUsd is a 6-decimal USD/TKN price and twaReserves[j] is the non-Bean reserve in its NATIVE decimals. The 1e18 numerator presumes the reserve is 1e18-scaled. For the out-of-season path it returns LibUsdOracle.getTokenPrice(token).mul(twaReserves[j]).div(1e6) — again assuming the reserve carries 18 decimals so the result lands at 1e18 USD precision.
  - getBeanTokenPriceFromTwaReserves (LibWell.sol#241-259): price = reserveBean.mul(1e18).div(reserveTkn) (or the inverse). The fixed 1e18 only yields a correctly-scaled TKN/BEAN price when Bean (6 dec) is paired against an 18-dec token; a 6-dec or 8-dec non-Bean token shifts the result by 10**(18-decimals).

These values are consumed by LibEvaluate.calcLPToSupplyRatio (usdLiquidity at LibEvaluate.sol#260, drives the L2SR weather case) and LibEvaluate.evalPrice (beanUsdPrice = 1e30 / (usdTokenPrice * beanTknPrice), LibEvaluate.sol#111-113, drives the excessive-price case 6). A non-18-decimal token would make usdLiquidity and beanUsdPrice wrong by a factor of 10**(18-decimals), pushing the L2SR/price weather cases into the wrong bucket and mis-sizing the season's stalk/soil/temperature response. This is a latent decimal-mismatch bug: currently inert because the live Wells use WETH/wstETH (both 18-dec), but it is triggered the moment governance whitelists a Well with a 6- or 8-decimal non-Bean token (e.g. USDC, WBTC).
findings.impact: If a Well with a non-18-decimal non-Bean token is whitelisted, the computed USD liquidity and Bean USD price are off by 10**(18-decimals). This corrupts the liquidity-to-supply ratio and the excessive-price detection in LibEvaluate, selecting the wrong Weather caseId and therefore mis-issuing grown stalk, soil, and temperature changes for that Season — a systematic accounting distortion of core monetary policy rather than a direct single-tx drain.
findings.recommendation: Normalize reserves to a common precision using the token's actual decimals (e.g. multiply by 10**(18 - IERC20Decimals(token).decimals())) before applying the 1e18 scaling, or enforce on whitelist (LibFertilizer.beginBarnRaiseMigration / whitelist path) that the non-Bean token has exactly 18 decimals and revert otherwise. Replace the hardcoded 1e18/1e6 constants in getWellTwaUsdLiquidityFromReserves and getBeanTokenPriceFromTwaReserves with decimal-aware scaling.

ite.intent: Cause Beanstalk to mis-evaluate the liquidity-to-supply ratio and Bean price for a Season, distorting stalk/soil/temperature issuance, by relying on a whitelisted Well whose non-Bean token is not 18 decimals.
ite.technique: After a non-18-dec token Well is whitelisted, sunrise->stepOracle stores native-decimal twaReserves; LibEvaluate.calcLPToSupplyRatio reads getWellTwaUsdLiquidityFromReserves (LibWell.sol#141/154 fixed 1e18/1e6) and evalPrice reads getBeanTokenPriceFromTwaReserves (LibWell.sol#250 fixed 1e18). The 10**(18-decimals) scale error flows into evalLpToSupplyRatio/evalPrice caseId selection and thus into LibGauge stalk/soil sizing.
ite.evasion: The code comments openly state 'assumes TKN has 18 decimals' but no whitelist check enforces it; the defense is purely conventional, so the first non-conforming Well silently produces wrong numbers.

findings.human_review_reason: Triggered only by a governance whitelisting action (adding a non-18-decimal Well token); impact is on monetary-policy accounting rather than a direct fund flow. Human should weigh likelihood of such a whitelist against Beanstalk's roadmap and confirm no upstream decimal normalization exists in the pump/well function.
critical_assumptions: Governance whitelists a Well whose non-Bean token has != 18 decimals (current Wells use 18-dec WETH/wstETH, so the bug is presently inert).

ice_chain.corrupted_state: usdLiquidity / beanUsdPrice computed in LibEvaluate from LibWell helpers
ice_chain.consumer_function: LibEvaluate.evalLpToSupplyRatio / LibEvaluate.evalPrice (-> Weather caseId -> LibGauge issuance)
ice_chain.consumer_action: Selects the Weather case that sets grown-stalk-per-season, soil, and temperature for the Season

findings.title: addMigratedUnderlying credits trusted amount, not measured balance diff
findings.description: UnripeFacet.addMigratedUnderlying (contracts/beanstalk/barn/UnripeFacet.sol#284-295) does safeTransferFrom(user, this, amount) then LibUnripe.incrementUnderlying(unripeToken, amount), crediting the caller-supplied `amount` rather than the actually-received balance delta. If the underlying token charges a fee-on-transfer or rebases down, balanceOfUnderlying is credited more than was received, breaking the invariant balanceOfUnderlying <= actual token balance and over-valuing chop/redemption math (unripeToUnderlying / _getUnderlying read balanceOfUnderlying). The same trust-the-amount pattern (vs the balance-diff accounting that LibTransfer.receiveToken uses) appears here. However the function is gated by LibDiamond.enforceIsContractOwner() and nonReentrant, the underlying token is owner-chosen, and it carries noNetFlow/noSupplyChange invariant guards, so this is a privileged-only correctness/operational concern, not a permissionless exploit.
findings.impact: Owner-only: if a fee-on-transfer/rebasing underlying is ever set, balanceOfUnderlying is over-credited, inflating per-unripe redemption (unripeToUnderlying) above the real backing. No permissionless path; requires owner to migrate to a non-standard underlying.
findings.recommendation: Measure the balance delta (balanceAfter - balanceBefore) and pass that to incrementUnderlying, mirroring LibTransfer.receiveToken's fee-on-transfer-safe accounting, instead of trusting `amount`.

ite.intent: (Privileged) Over-credit Unripe Token underlying backing if a fee-on-transfer underlying is migrated in, inflating later redemptions.
ite.technique: addMigratedUnderlying transfers `amount` then incrementUnderlying(amount) without measuring received balance (UnripeFacet.sol#289-294).
ite.evasion: enforceIsContractOwner + nonReentrant + noNetFlow gate the function; the residual gap is only the unmeasured FoT delta, reachable solely by the owner choosing a non-standard underlying.

critical_assumptions: Contract owner is the caller (function is enforceIsContractOwner-gated).
The migrated underlying token is fee-on-transfer or rebasing (standard ERC-20 underlying credits correctly).

ice_chain.consumer_action: Pays out underlying proportional to inflated balanceOfUnderlying
